RULE-21 (em dash) IS A GLYPH ARTEFACT, NOT A TIC — the single most important falsification of this run. Morrowind's text is ASCII and writes the dash as '--': books 20.37 per 10k, dialogue 19.04, journal 9.53. We write U+2014 and never '--'. Comparing the CHARACTER gives books 51x, dialogue inf (they have literally zero U+2014), journal inf. Comparing the FIGURE (any of — – -- ' - ') gives books 38.66 vs 21.87 = 1.8x, dialogue 17.69 vs 20.17 = 0.9x, journal 3.21 vs 9.85 = 0.3x. In dialogue and journal we use the dash figure LESS than Morrowind. Swapping — for -- would take a one-token detector from inf to 1.0 while changing not one word of the writing: it is the exact 'same fingerprint in a hat' move the brief forbids, and it is why the fix here is (a) report the confound and (b) trim only the genuine books over-use.

BOOKS dash pass: 35 line markers stripped by tools/prose/strip-line-markers.mjs (a dash used as a bullet/ledger rule is layout, not prose, and Morrowind never does it) + 14 authored layout rewrites. Books dash FIGURE now 24.46 vs ref 21.87 = 1.1x, i.e. parity. Did NOT rewrite the rhetorical asides: Morrowind uses the same figure at the same rate, spelled '--'. NOTE a real bug found in my own tool by its regression test: the first version matched an ESCAPED quote inside prose and silently stripped an inline dash out of marginalia-in-a-borrowed-book; fixed with a (?<!\\) lookbehind, dash restored, regression test added.

THE RESIDUAL 'ELEVEN' IN THE JOURNAL IS A DESIGN FACT, NOT A PROSE TIC — and this is the most interesting thing in the run. After the filler is gone, every remaining eleven is plot arithmetic a player can count: eleven live roots, eleven keepers at eleven wells, eleven burial boxes, eleven steps to the reservoir floor, eleven unwritten porters at eleven gold a week, eleven hundred in the box, 611 leased, 411 on the register, eleven names, eleven leaves in four hundred years. The machine's favourite number did not stay in the prose — it became the main quest's central motif. Renumbering it is a DESIGN change touching quests, states and a sealed answer, and is out of scope for a prose pass; it is flagged for the owner instead.

SPOKEN-REGISTER BASELINE - MY CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS FALSIFIED, and this is the interesting half. Our dialogue is NOT more literary than Morrowind's. SR-09 abstract nominalisation ours 100.94 vs ref 131.33 = 0.8x (THEY use more); SR-11 front-loaded subordinate clause 0.4x (they use more); SR-10 formal subordinator ZERO in ours; SR-12 hedge 1.0x parity; SR-17 semicolon/colon 1.1x; SR-18 mean words/sentence 11.22 vs 10.28 = 1.09x and part of even that 9% is the contraction artefact above. Long Latinate sentences are not the defect. SR-13 imperative opener 1.7x ours HIGHER, also against prior.

WHAT THE DEFECT ACTUALLY IS: every rule that DID separate is a marker of a person reacting to another person, and all point one way. Exclamation 0.34 vs 21.25 per 10k (62x fewer); question mark 19.26 vs 158.83 (8x fewer); sentence-initial And/But/So 7.57 vs 77.09 (10x fewer); discourse opener (well/now/look/listen) 11.87 vs 29.97; first-person I/me/my 153.05 vs 329.50 (2x fewer); second person you/your 377.98 vs 454.32; contractions 16.68 vs 327.78 (20x fewer). Our NPCs do not read as literary - they read as UNINVOLVED. Nobody in our dialogue exclaims, asks back, or says 'I'. That is a voice defect no regex can fix.

THE ANSWER TO THE BRIEF'S ACTUAL QUESTION, once my own bAcc bug is corrected (see next finding): a mechanical contraction swap would have taken SR-01 from 0.844 to ~0.50 and left SR-08 (sentence-initial conjunction, contraction-blind) standing at 0.822 separation. The hat move buys 0.022. That is the quantified value of the shortcut the brief forbids, and it is nearly zero.

MY SUMMARY STATISTIC WAS WRONG AND I CAUGHT IT BY READING MY OWN OUTPUT. separation() scores 'rule fires => ours', so a rule MORROWIND uses more scores BELOW 0.5 - and the first run read that as 'does not separate', reporting BLIND-GAP +0.271. It is the opposite: bAcc 0.178 for sentence-initial And/But/So means 'fires => Morrowind' is right 82.2% of the time. Every rule that most exposes our dialogue points that way. Corrected to a direction-agnostic max(bAcc, 1-bAcc) with the direction printed.

THE BRIEF'S QUESTION, ANSWERED WITH A NUMBER: BLIND-GAP was +0.022 at baseline. The best contraction-movable separator (SR-01, 0.844) beat the best contraction-BLIND one (SR-08 sentence-initial And/But/So, 0.822) by 0.022. So the sed fix - do not -> don't - would have taken the headline rule to ~0.50 and left an equally strong separator standing untouched. The shortcut the brief forbids was worth 0.022 of separation. That is the quantified case against it.
